elements: Defendant drove, operated, or was in actual physical control of a motor vehicle
Within the State of Oklahoma
While under the influence of alcohol, any intoxicating substance, or a combination
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
enhancements: Child under 18 in vehicle (child endangerment enhancement)
Third or subsequent offense within 10 years (felony)
notes: Implied consent under § 11-902(A). Admin license revocation 180 days first offense. Ignition interlock required. Oklahoma has a 10-year look-back period for enhancement purposes. Aggravated DUI (BAC .15+) carries enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or intoxicating substance
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
No prior DUI convictions within 10 years
mandatory_minimum: 10 days imprisonment or community service; substance abuse assessment
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (aggravated — mandatory 1 year interlock)
notes: License revocation 180 days. Ignition interlock device may be required. Must complete substance abuse assessment and recommended treatment.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or intoxicating substance
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
One or more prior DUI convictions within 10 years
notes: Second offense: 1-5 year license revocation. Third offense: 3-year revocation. Mandatory ignition interlock for all repeat offenders. GPS monitoring may be ordered.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of any intoxicating substance other than alcohol
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and any other intoxicating substance
To a degree rendering the defendant incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se drug limit. Prosecution must prove impairment. Includes prescription medications. Blood or urine test may be required under implied consent.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In a careless or wanton manner without regard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. Adds points to driving record. May result in license suspension.

statute_title: Leaving the Scene of an Accident — Injury or Death
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury or death to any person
Defendant failed to immediately stop at the scene
Defendant failed to render aid and provide identification
notes: Property damage only is a misdemeanor under § 10-103. Leaving scene involving death can result in enhanced penalties. Must report to nearest law enforcement.

statute_title: DUI Causing Death — First Degree Manslaughter
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or intoxicating substance
Defendant's intoxicated driving caused the death of another person
notes: DUI-related deaths prosecuted as first-degree manslaughter under Okla. Stat. tit. 21 § 711. Penalties are severe with mandatory minimum. May also be charged as second-degree murder in egregious cases.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
While operating a motor vehicle in a negligent or reckless manner
Or while committing a misdemeanor offense (DUI)
notes: Oklahoma charges vehicular deaths under the general manslaughter statute. If DUI-related, charged as first-degree manslaughter (misdemeanor-manslaughter rule). Non-DUI vehicular deaths may be second-degree manslaughter.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended, Revoked, or Denied
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was suspended, revoked, canceled, or denied
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension
notes: Driving on DUI-related suspension is a felony. Additional suspension period imposed. May require SR-22 insurance filing.

elements: A peace officer signaled the defendant to stop
Signal was given by hand, voice, siren, or light
Defendant willfully attempted to elude or flee from the officer
Defendant knew or should have known the person was a peace officer
notes: Eluding causing injury or death is a felony with substantially enhanced penalties. License revocation mandatory. Commonly charged alongside other traffic offenses.

statute_title: Possession of a Controlled Dangerous Substance
offense_class: Misdemeanor (simple possession under SQ 780); Felony (distribution quantities)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
A controlled dangerous substance
Without a valid prescription or legal authorization
notes: State Question 780 (2016) reclassified simple drug possession from felony to misdemeanor. Applies to personal-use amounts only. Distribution quantities remain felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
Marijuana
Without a valid medical marijuana license
notes: Oklahoma legalized medical marijuana in 2018 (SQ 788). Personal possession without a medical card remains a misdemeanor under SQ 780. Growing without a license is a felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
Cocaine or crack cocaine (Schedule II)
Without a valid prescription
notes: Simple possession reclassified to misdemeanor under SQ 780. Distribution quantities or intent to distribute remain felonies. Cocaine is Schedule II in Oklahoma.

elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
Methamphetamine (Schedule II)
Without a valid prescription
notes: Simple possession reclassified to misdemeanor under SQ 780. Manufacturing meth remains a serious felony under § 2-401. Oklahoma has anti-meth manufacturing provisions restricting pseudoephedrine purchases.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, transported, or distributed
A controlled substance in a trafficking quantity
Quantity met or exceeded statutory trafficking thresholds
notes: Trafficking thresholds: marijuana 25+ lbs, cocaine 28g+, meth 20g+, heroin 10g+. Mandatory minimum sentences. No suspended sentence for trafficking. 85% rule applies — must serve 85% before parole eligibility.

statute_title: Distribution of a Controlled Dangerous Substance
penalty_max: Life (Schedule I-II); 10 years (Schedule III-IV); 5 years (Schedule V)
elements: Defendant knowingly distributed, dispensed, or possessed with intent to distribute
A controlled dangerous substance
To another person
Without legal authorization
notes: Distribution to minors doubles the penalty. Second offense doubles the applicable range. Distribution near schools carries mandatory enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured or attempted to manufacture
A controlled dangerous substance
Without legal authorization
mandatory_minimum: 7 years (meth manufacturing); 20 years (if child present during meth manufacturing)
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of a minor (20 years mandatory)
notes: Methamphetamine manufacturing carries especially severe penalties. Manufacturing in presence of a child under 12 is 20 years mandatory minimum. Cleanup costs assessed to defendant.

elements: Defendant knowingly used or possessed with intent to use
Drug paraphernalia
For the purpose of ingesting, inhaling, or otherwise introducing a controlled substance into the body
enhancements: Distribution of paraphernalia to a minor (felony)
notes: Reclassified to misdemeanor under SQ 780. Distribution of paraphernalia is a separate offense. Distribution to a minor is a felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled dangerous substance
With the intent to manufacture, distribute, or dispense
Intent may be inferred from quantity, packaging, or other evidence
notes: Intent inferred from circumstantial evidence including quantity, packaging, scales, cash, and communications. Same penalties as distribution.

elements: Defendant deliberately and with premeditation caused the death of another person
Or caused death during the commission of a forcible felony (felony murder)
enhancements: Victim was a child, law enforcement officer, or other protected person
notes: Oklahoma has the death penalty. Aggravating circumstances must be found for death sentence. Felony murder applies during commission of certain forcible felonies.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With imminently dangerous conduct evincing a depraved mind
Without premeditation or during commission of certain felonies
notes: Second degree murder includes depraved-mind murder (reckless conduct showing extreme indifference to human life) and certain felony murders not qualifying as first degree.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
In the heat of passion upon adequate provocation
Without premeditation or malice aforethought
notes: First degree manslaughter includes heat-of-passion killings and deaths during misdemeanor offenses. Mandatory minimum 4 years. No suspended or deferred sentence.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Through culpable negligence
Without intent to kill
notes: Second degree manslaughter covers unintentional killings resulting from criminal negligence. Less culpable than first degree. Vehicular deaths without DUI may be charged here.

statute_title: Assault and Battery with a Dangerous Weapon
elements: Defendant willfully caused bodily injury to another person
With a dangerous or deadly weapon
Or with intent to cause great bodily harm
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer or emergency responder
notes: Includes assault with a dangerous weapon, intent to kill, and shooting with intent to kill (§ 652). Penalties vary by specific subsection and circumstances.

elements: Defendant willfully and unlawfully attempted or threatened
To commit a violent injury upon another person
With the apparent ability to carry out the threat
notes: Simple assault without battery (no physical contact). Assault AND battery is a separate offense under § 644.

elements: Defendant willfully and unlawfully used force or violence upon another person
enhancements: Against a law enforcement officer (felony under § 649)
notes: Oklahoma combines assault and battery into one offense. Simple assault and battery is a misdemeanor. Enhanced versions include battery on officers, the elderly, and children.

elements: Defendant took personal property of another from the person or immediate presence
By means of force or fear
Against the will of the victim
enhancements: Armed with a dangerous weapon (armed robbery)
notes: Robbery by force or fear without a weapon. Armed robbery is a separate, more serious offense under § 801.

statute_title: Robbery with a Dangerous Weapon (Armed Robbery)
elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a firearm or other dangerous weapon
Or the defendant or an accomplice displayed or threatened the use of a weapon
enhancements: Use of a firearm (additional mandatory minimum)
notes: Armed robbery carries a 5-year mandatory minimum. Must serve 85% before parole eligibility. One of the most severely punished property crimes in Oklahoma.

penalty_max: Life (without parole if for extortion or ransom)
elements: Defendant seized, confined, inveigled, decoyed, kidnapped, abducted, or carried away another person
By any means whatsoever
With intent to hold for ransom, extort money, commit a felony, or inflict bodily injury
enhancements: For purpose of extortion or ransom
notes: Kidnapping for extortion or ransom is punishable by life without parole or death (in extreme cases). Must serve 85% of sentence before parole eligibility.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously set fire to or burned
An occupied dwelling, building, or structure
Or aided, counseled, or procured the burning
notes: First degree arson involves occupied or insured structures. Second degree arson (§ 1402) covers unoccupied structures. Third degree (§ 1403) covers personal property. Arson causing death may be charged as first-degree murder.

elements: Defendant intended to cause the death of another person
Defendant performed an overt act toward the commission of murder
The act went beyond mere preparation
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Attempted first-degree murder carries up to life imprisonment. Shooting with intent to kill (§ 652) is a related but distinct charge.

elements: Defendant assaulted another person
With a deadly or dangerous weapon
With intent to do bodily harm
notes: Distinct from shooting with intent to kill (§ 652). Deadly weapon includes firearms, knives, and any object used in a manner capable of causing death.

elements: Defendant took personal property of another
Without the owner's consent
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: SQ 780 raised the felony threshold from $500 to $1,000. Larceny of merchandise from a retailer is covered under § 1731.

elements: Defendant took personal property of another
Value exceeded $1,000
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Grand larceny is theft of property valued over $1,000 (threshold raised by SQ 780 from $500). Prior convictions may enhance penalties.

elements: Defendant took personal property of another
Value was under $1,000
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: SQ 780 raised the petit/grand larceny threshold from $500 to $1,000. Multiple petit larceny convictions may enhance subsequent offenses to felony.

statute_title: Larceny of Merchandise from a Retailer (Shoplifting)
elements: Defendant took merchandise from a retail establishment
Without paying the full purchase price
With intent to deprive the retailer
notes: Includes concealment of merchandise, price tag alteration, and transfer between containers. Civil liability to merchant also applies.

elements: Defendant broke and entered a dwelling house of another
In which a human being was present at the time
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: First degree burglary requires occupied dwelling. Second degree (§ 1435) covers unoccupied buildings and structures. Must serve 85% of first-degree burglary sentence.

elements: Defendant broke and entered a dwelling house
A human being was present at the time of the entry
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Same as first degree burglary. Human presence at time of entry is the key element distinguishing first from second degree. 85% rule applies.

statute_title: Unauthorized Use of a Motor Vehicle
elements: Defendant took, drove, or used a motor vehicle belonging to another
Without the owner's consent
With intent to temporarily or permanently deprive the owner
notes: May also be charged as grand larceny if value exceeds $1,000 (virtually all vehicles). Separate statute for unauthorized use emphasizes taking without consent.

elements: Defendant received, concealed, or aided in concealing property
Knowing or having reasonable cause to believe it was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Same felony/misdemeanor threshold as larceny ($1,000 under SQ 780). Knowledge of stolen status may be inferred from circumstances.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously damaged or destroyed property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: SQ 780 raised the felony threshold to $1,000 in property damage. Restitution commonly ordered in addition to criminal penalties.

elements: Defendant entered or remained upon the land or premises of another
Without permission or lawful authority
After notice that entry was prohibited
enhancements: Trespass with intent to commit a crime (burglary)
notes: Notice may be given by posting signs, fencing, or verbal communication. Trespass on critical infrastructure carries enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Malicious Injury and Destruction of Property
elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously injured or destroyed property of another
notes: Same statute as vandalism. Oklahoma uses 'malicious injury to property' rather than 'criminal mischief.'

elements: Defendant committed assault and battery
Against a current or former spouse, partner, parent of a shared child, or household member
notes: Domestic assault by strangulation was added as a specific felony in 2017. First offense requires completion of batterer's intervention program. Protective orders available under 22 O.S. § 60.

statute_title: Domestic Assault and Battery — First Offense
elements: Defendant committed assault and battery upon a family or household member
notes: Oklahoma combines assault and battery into one offense. First domestic offense is a misdemeanor. Mandatory batterer's intervention program.

elements: Defendant knowingly permitted a child to be present where controlled substances are manufactured or stored
Or exposed a child to the risk of serious harm or death
Through criminal negligence
enhancements: Drug manufacturing in presence of child (mandatory 20 years)
notes: Broad statute covering exposure to drugs, DUI with child passenger, and general endangerment. Especially severe penalties when linked to drug manufacturing.

elements: Defendant willfully or maliciously injured, tortured, or maimed a child under 18
Or used unreasonable force upon a child
notes: Child abuse causing serious injury can carry life sentence. Mandatory reporting by certain professionals under tit. 10A § 1-2-101. Child neglect is a separate offense under § 843.5(C).

elements: A valid protective order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated a term of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation within 10 years (felony)
notes: First violation carries mandatory minimum 20 days jail. Second violation within 10 years is a felony. GPS monitoring may be ordered.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (subsequent or with threat of death)
elements: Defendant willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly followed or harassed another person
In a manner that would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or threatened
Defendant made a credible threat with intent to place the person in fear of death or great bodily harm
enhancements: Violation of protective order during stalking (felony)
Threat of death or bodily harm
notes: Includes cyberstalking. First offense without threat of bodily harm is a misdemeanor. Protective orders may be issued alongside criminal charges.

elements: Defendant contacted another person by telephone, electronic means, or mail
With intent to terrify, intimidate, threaten, or harass
The communication placed the victim in reasonable fear
notes: Includes telephone harassment, electronic harassment, and threatening communications. May escalate to stalking if conduct is repeated.

elements: Defendant willfully abused, neglected, or exploited a vulnerable adult
Victim was an incapacitated or vulnerable adult
Defendant was a caregiver or person responsible for the victim's welfare
notes: Vulnerable adult includes elderly and disabled persons. Financial exploitation is increasingly prosecuted. Mandatory reporting by certain professionals.

elements: Defendant carried a weapon on their person or in a vehicle
Under circumstances prohibited by law
enhancements: Carry in prohibited location (bars, schools, government buildings)
notes: Oklahoma enacted constitutional carry (permitless carry) in 2019 (HB 2597). Most adults 21+ can carry without a permit. Prohibited locations include bars, schools, courthouses, and government buildings. Some restrictions remain for ages 18-20.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had a prior felony conviction
enhancements: Possession during commission of another crime
notes: Includes adjudicated delinquent felonies. Federal 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) also applies. Oklahoma allows some felons to possess firearms after completing sentence and waiting period for non-violent offenses.

elements: Defendant carried a firearm or weapon
In a location prohibited by law (school, bar, courthouse, etc.)
notes: Constitutional carry enacted in 2019 but prohibited locations still apply. Carrying in a bar while consuming alcohol is specifically prohibited. Schools and government buildings remain gun-free zones.

elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
In a reckless or negligent manner
Without regard for the safety of others
notes: Includes celebratory gunfire and negligent discharges. Discharge resulting in injury may be charged as assault with a deadly weapon.

elements: Defendant willfully and with fraudulent intent obtained, possessed, transferred, or used
Identifying information of another person
Without that person's consent
For the purpose of committing or aiding any unlawful act
notes: Fine up to $100,000. Restitution ordered. Includes use of another's name, SSN, birth date, driver's license number, or biometric data.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with property belonging to another
By virtue of employment, office, or position of trust
Defendant fraudulently converted the property to personal use
notes: Oklahoma has a specific embezzlement statute. Public officer embezzlement is separately addressed under § 1452. SQ 780 raised the felony threshold to $1,000.

elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud
Falsely made, altered, forged, or counterfeited a written instrument
Or knowingly uttered a forged instrument
notes: First degree forgery involves instruments that evidence rights or obligations (checks, deeds, contracts). Second degree forgery (§ 1577) covers less significant instruments.

elements: Defendant made, forged, or counterfeited currency, coins, or obligations
With intent to defraud
notes: Most currency counterfeiting is prosecuted federally. State charges may apply to counterfeit documents, tickets, or other instruments of value.

statute_title: Bogus Check — Issuing Check Without Sufficient Funds
elements: Defendant made, drew, issued, or delivered a check
Knowing at the time there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: SQ 780 raised felony threshold to $1,000. Written demand and failure to pay within 10 days creates presumption of intent. First-time offenders may qualify for diversion.

elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented
A false or fraudulent claim or material misrepresentation
To an insurance company
For the purpose of obtaining payment or benefit
notes: Oklahoma Insurance Fraud Bureau investigates claims. Includes auto, health, property, and workers' compensation fraud. Restitution required.

statute_title: Credit Card or Debit Card Fraud
elements: Defendant knowingly used a credit or debit card
Without the cardholder's authorization
To obtain money, goods, or services by fraud
notes: Oklahoma has specific credit card fraud statutes. Includes theft of card, fraudulent use, and trafficking in stolen cards. Federal charges common for interstate transactions.

elements: Defendant knowingly conducted a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of unlawful activity
With intent to promote criminal activity or disguise the source of funds
notes: Often charged alongside drug trafficking. Asset forfeiture provisions apply. Fine can be up to twice the amount laundered. Federal charges common.

statute_title: Obtaining Money or Property by False Pretenses (Fraud)
elements: Defendant obtained money, property, or a valuable thing from another
By means of false pretense, representation, or fraud
With intent to cheat or defraud
notes: General fraud catch-all statute. SQ 780 raised felony threshold to $1,000. Specific fraud statutes may apply for particular types of fraud.

elements: Defendant committed an act of sexual intercourse with another person
By force, violence, or threats
Or with a person incapable of consent due to mental illness, intoxication, or unconsciousness
Or with a victim under 14
notes: Oklahoma is one of few states authorizing death for rape of a child under 14 (though constitutionality is unsettled). Lifetime sex offender registration required. 85% rule applies.

elements: Defendant committed an act of sexual intercourse with another person
Victim was between 14 and 16 and defendant was over 18
Or victim was intoxicated by an administered substance
Or consent was given under duress
notes: Second degree rape covers statutory situations and some non-violent but non-consensual encounters. Sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Felony (subsequent or exposure to minor)
elements: Defendant willfully exposed their person in a public place
In a lewd or indecent manner
notes: First offense is a misdemeanor. Subsequent offenses or exposure to minors are felonies. May require sex offender registration.

elements: Defendant offered or agreed to engage in sexual conduct
In exchange for money or other consideration
Or solicited another to engage in prostitution
notes: Soliciting a minor is charged as human trafficking under § 748. Near school/church enhancement makes it a felony. STD testing may be required.

statute_title: Sexual Exploitation of a Child (Child Pornography)
elements: Defendant knowingly produced, possessed, or distributed
Material depicting a minor under 18 engaged in sexual conduct
Defendant knew or should have known the person depicted was a minor
notes: Federal charges commonly apply. Oklahoma law covers production, distribution, and possession. 85% rule applies to production charges. Sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register under the Sex Offenders Registration Act
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update registration
Within the time period required by law
notes: Must register within 3 business days of establishing residence. Verification required every 90 days (habitual/aggravated) or annually. Failure to comply is a separate felony.

statute_title: Rape — Victim Under Age of Consent
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse with a minor
Victim was below the age of consent (16)
Defendant was the age specified by the applicable statute
notes: Age of consent is 16 in Oklahoma. Under 14 with defendant over 18 is first degree rape. 14-16 with defendant over 18 is second degree rape. Sex offender registration required.

elements: Defendant willfully and wrongfully disturbed the peace of others
By engaging in fighting, violent behavior, or loud/unreasonable noise
Or used obscene or threatening language in a public place
notes: Broad catch-all offense. Commonly charged alongside other offenses. Oklahoma also has specific noise ordinances in municipalities.

elements: Defendant willfully resisted, delayed, or obstructed
A public officer in the discharge of official duties
notes: Resisting by physical force may be charged as assault and battery on a police officer (§ 649), a felony. Verbal objection alone is not sufficient.

statute_title: Obstructing Justice / Obstruction of an Officer
elements: Defendant willfully hindered, delayed, or obstructed
A peace officer in the discharge of official duties
Or aided a person in escaping arrest or prosecution
enhancements: Accessory after the fact to a felony (felony under § 175)
notes: Includes hiding evidence, providing false information to officers, and harboring fugitives. Accessory after the fact to a felony is a separate, more serious offense.

offense_class: Varies — up to 6 months per count for criminal contempt
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disorderly behavior in the presence of the court
Or interfered with court proceedings
notes: Includes both direct (in presence of court) and indirect (violation of court order) contempt. Court has broad discretion. Due process protections apply to criminal contempt.

elements: Defendant appeared in a public place
Under the influence of alcohol or drugs
In a condition that posed a direct danger to self or others or was otherwise incapacitated
notes: Law enforcement may take intoxicated persons to a detox facility rather than jail. Chronic offenders may be referred to treatment programs.

elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
notes: Bond may be forfeited and bench warrant issued. Bail jumping in a felony case is a separate felony. Sentence runs consecutive to any sentence in the underlying case.

elements: Defendant knowingly communicated false information
To a law enforcement officer
Regarding the commission of a crime
notes: Includes filing false police reports, false 911 calls, and false accusations. False bomb threats are charged under separate, more serious statutes.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (basic); Felony (threat to bomb or attack school/government)
elements: Defendant threatened to commit an act of violence
Against another person or property
With intent to place another in fear of serious harm
enhancements: Threat against school or government building
notes: Bomb threats and threats against schools carry felony charges. Electronic threats (email, text, social media) are covered. Need not have actual intent to carry out threat.

elements: Defendant made a willful and corrupt false statement
Under oath or affirmation
In a judicial proceeding or before an authorized officer
On a matter material to the issue in question
notes: Subornation of perjury (inducing another to commit perjury) is the same offense class. Corroboration typically required. False statements outside judicial proceedings may be charged under § 504.

elements: Defendant offered, gave, or promised money or thing of value
To a public official or public servant
With intent to influence the official's action, decision, or vote
notes: Both the giver and receiver can be charged. Bribery of jurors (§ 383) and witnesses (§ 386) are separate offenses. Public official permanently disqualified from office.

elements: Defendant was in lawful custody or confinement
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from custody
enhancements: Escape from prison (§ 438 — up to life)
notes: Escape from state penitentiary carries up to life imprisonment under § 438. Sentence runs consecutive to original sentence. Assisting escape is a separate felony.

elements: Defendant willfully or maliciously tortured, maimed, or killed an animal
Or failed to provide adequate food, water, or shelter
notes: Aggravated cruelty (torture, mutilation, malicious killing) is a felony. Animal fighting is a separate felony. Court may order forfeiture of animals and psychological evaluation.

offense_class: Varies — court may revoke and impose original sentence
penalty_max: Original sentence for the underlying offense
fine_max: Original fine for the underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation with specific conditions
Defendant violated one or more conditions of probation
Violation was willful and without valid excuse
notes: Court may continue probation, modify conditions, or revoke. Hearing required. Burden of proof is preponderance of evidence. Technical violations distinguished from new criminal conduct.

offense_class: Varies — Pardon and Parole Board may revoke parole
elements: Defendant was released on parole with specific conditions
Defendant violated one or more conditions of parole
notes: Oklahoma Pardon and Parole Board determines revocation. Revocation hearing required. May serve remainder of sentence. New criminal conduct typically results in revocation.

elements: Defendant aided, abetted, counseled, or encouraged another person
In planning or committing a criminal offense
With intent to promote or facilitate the commission of the offense
notes: Oklahoma treats all participants in a crime equally (§ 172). Principals and accessories before the fact are punished the same. Accessory after the fact (§ 175) is a separate, lesser offense.

offense_class: Same as the target offense (Oklahoma punishes attempt the same as completed crime)
elements: Defendant intended to commit a specific offense
Defendant performed an overt act toward the commission of the offense
The act went beyond mere preparation
notes: Oklahoma is unusual in that attempt carries the same penalty as the completed offense under § 44. Every person who attempts to commit a crime and performs an overt act is punishable as if the crime were committed.

offense_class: Same as the target offense (or as specifically provided)
penalty_max: Same as the target offense or 10 years (whichever applies)
elements: Two or more persons agreed to commit a crime
At least one overt act was committed in furtherance of the conspiracy
Defendant intended that the crime be committed
notes: Oklahoma conspiracy penalties vary based on the target offense. Conspiracy to commit a felony is itself a felony. Requires an overt act by any co-conspirator.
